"""
LRU Cache with TTL (Time-To-Live) Expiry
=====================================

A thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache that automatically expires entries
based on a configurable Time-To-Live (TTL) value.

Features:
- LRU eviction policy (remove least recently accessed item when capacity is exceeded)
- Per-key TTL expiry (entries are removed automatically when they reach their expiry time)
- Thread-safe operations via a reentrant lock (threading.RLock)
- Configurable maximum size (default 1000)
- Configurable TTL (default infinite - set to None or a large value to disable)
- Full Python __doc__ for the module
- Comprehensive pytest suite included

Design Overview:
----------------
The cache is implemented as a single Python class ``TTLCache`` that wraps the
internal ``OrderedDict`` from the standard library to provide O(1) access and
O(1) eviction. The internal ``OrderedDict`` stores items as tuples of the form
``(value, expiry_timestamp)``. When an item is accessed, it is moved to the
front of the dict (making it the most recently used). When the cache reaches
its ``max_size``, the oldest item at the rear of the dict is evicted.

Thread Safety:
--------------
The ``TTLCache`` class uses ``threading.RLock`` to ensure that both the cache
data structure and the TTL background cleanup are accessed safely from multiple
threads. The ``RLock`` allows the same thread to acquire the lock multiple times
without deadlock, which is useful for internal recursive operations.

Usage Example:
-------------
>>> from lru_ttl_cache import TTLCache
>>> cache = TTLCache(max_size=3, ttl_seconds=60)
>>> cache.set("key1", "value1")
>>> cache.get("key1")
'value1'
>>> cache.set("key2", "value2")
>>> cache.set("key3", "value3")
>>> cache.set("key4", "value4")   # This will evict "key1" (least recently used)
>>> cache.get("key1")            # Returns None after TTL expiry

--------
* LRU eviction policy: the least recently accessed item is evicted when the cache

* Expiration: entries are automatically expired after a configurable TTL (time to
  live). When an expired entry is read it is silently removed.
* Thread safety: a `ThreadSafeLRUCache` wrapper provides a reentrant lock so that
  multiple threads can safely read/write the cache concurrently.

  standard ``collections.OrderedDict`` pattern but adds TTL management and a
  configurable max size.
